title: Eyes on the Milky Way
caption: An Auxiliary Telescope under the Milky Way, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: An Auxiliary Telescope, one of four serving ESO's Very Large Telescope, looks up at the sky above Paranal Observatory. Overhead, the Milky Way shows as a bright band across the southern sky.

The Auxiliary Telescopes send their light into the Very Large Telescope Interferometer, or VLTI. Combining light from several telescopes increases the amount of data collected and sharpens the images the system can produce.

Paranal sits 2600 meters up in Chile's Atacama Desert and enjoys about 300 clear nights a year. These conditions make it an excellent place to observe, and Carlos Fairbairn's photograph shows how clearly our own galaxy can be seen from there, stretching as a bright band right across the whole sky of the southern hemisphere.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera at an ESO site, in visible light. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long camera exposure gathers far more light than the eye can, so the Milky Way and faint stars appear brighter and richer than they would to someone standing there.
